rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets remembering the Lord as remembering one's return and standing before Him, which leads one to pray to Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه فصلى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's reading and organizes religious action into purifying belief, knowing God, and serving Him.
rows.anchor: وأقول : هذا التفسير متعين وذلك لأن مراتب أعمال المكلف ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first stage, removing false beliefs from the heart, is what the preceding verse calls purification.
rows.anchor: فالمرتبة الأولى : هي المراد بالتزكية في قوله : { قد أفلح من تزكى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second stage is knowing God in His essence, attributes, and names; remembrance in the heart is knowledge.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : هي المراد بقوله : { وذكر اسم ربه } فإن الذكر بالقلب ليس إلا المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third stage is service to God, expressed by prayer as humility and submissiveness.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : الخدمة وهي المراد بقوله : { فصلى } فإن الصلاة عبارة عن التواضع والخشوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing God's majesty must show itself in bodily acts of submission and humility.
rows.anchor: فمن استنار قلبه بمعرفة جلال الله تعالى وكبريائه

rows.speaker: عكرمة وأبو العالية وابن سيرين وابن عمر
rows.claim: These authorities read the passage as giving alms before going to the Eid prayer, then praying Eid with the imam.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول عكرمة وأبي العالية وابن سيرين وابن عمر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Eid-alms and Eid-prayer interpretation is also narrated as a report raised to the Prophet; al-Rāzī states no grading.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك مرفوعا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that the Eid reading puts alms before prayer, whereas the Qurʾān customarily mentions prayer before zakat.
rows.anchor: أن عادة الله تعالى في القرآن تقديم ذكر الصلاة على ذكر الزكاة لا تقديم الزكاة على الصلاة

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī says the sūra is Meccan by consensus, when neither Eid nor zakat al-fiṭr existed in Mecca; al-Rāzī uses this as an objection.
rows.anchor: قال الثعلبي : هذه السورة مكية بالإجماع ولم يكن بمكة عيد ولا زكاة فطر

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī replies that God may praise people for a practice He knows will occur later.
rows.anchor: أجاب الواحدي عنه بأنه لا يمتنع أن يقال

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil reads purification as giving from one's wealth and remembering God through affirming His oneness in prayer.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : { قد أفلح من تزكى } أي تصدق من ماله وذكر ربه بالتوحيد في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the Eid interpretation, Muqātil's reading concerns the obligatory alms and prayers.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين هذا الوجه وما قبله أن هذا يتناول الزكاة والصلاة المفروضتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes purification as cleansing one's deeds of ostentation and deficiency, rather than paying zakat on wealth; ordinary usage says wealth is zakā, not tazakkā.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد منه زكاة المال بل زكاة الأعمال أي من تطهر في أعماله من الرياء والتقصير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further report from Ibn ʿAbbās takes this as proclaiming God's greatness while setting out for Eid.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { وذكر اسم ربه } أي كبر في خروجه إلى العيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In that further interpretation, the prayer is the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: كبر في خروجه إلى العيد وصلى صلاة العيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is remembering God during prayer, unlike hypocrites who pray ostentatiously and remember God only rarely.
rows.anchor: المعنى وذكر اسم ربه في صلاته ولا تكون صلاته كصلاة المنافقين

rows.speaker: الفقهاء
rows.claim: Jurists cite the verse as evidence that the opening takbīr is obligatory.
rows.anchor: الفقهاء احتجوا بهذه الآية على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues that the conjunction separates the opening takbīr from prayer, so it is not part of prayer.
rows.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة رحمه الله بها على أن تكبيرة الافتتاح

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa also argues that the opening is valid with any of God's names.
rows.anchor: واحتج أيضا بهذه الآية على أن الافتتاح جائز بكل اسم من أسمائه

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī's school replies that the wording can be understood as 'he prayed, then remembered God's name'; ordinary speech can reverse the order.
rows.anchor: وأجاب أصحابنا بأن تقدير الآية

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa answers that the sequential force of the fāʾ cannot be set aside without evidence.
rows.anchor: ولأبي حنيفة أن يقول : ترك العمل بفاء التعقيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī's preferred reply is that the verse praises remembering God and then praying, without identifying the remembrance as the opening takbīr.
rows.anchor: الأولى ) في الجواب أن يقال : الآية تدل على مدح كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remembrance may instead be inward recollection of God's reward and punishment, which prompts prayer; takbīr is then one component of the prayer.
rows.anchor: فلعل المراد به أن من ذكر الله بقلبه وذكر ثوابه وعقابه دعاه ذلك إلى فعل الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The things sworn by must have religious benefit as signs of divine oneness, worldly benefit that calls for gratitude, or both; interpreters differ according to what they judge most important.
rows.anchor: لابد وأن يكون فيها إما فائدة دينية مثل كونها دلائل باهرة على التوحيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies al-fajr as the familiar dawn, the breaking of true or false dawn.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس أن الفجر هو الصبح المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn ends night, reveals light, and sends people and animals out seeking provision, making it a sign of resurrection from graves.
rows.anchor: لما يحصل به من انقضاء الليل وظهور الضوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emergence of creatures at dawn resembles the resurrection of the dead and offers a lesson to anyone who reflects.
rows.anchor: وذلك مشاكل لنشور الموتى من قبورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī connects the oath by dawn with other dawn and morning passages and with God's description as the maker of daybreak.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله : { والصبح إذا أسفر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpreters take dawn's beginning as a designation for the whole daytime, as in the oaths by forenoon and by day as it becomes clear.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال المراد به جميع النهار إلا أنه دل بالابتداء على الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes al-fajr to mean the dawn prayer, which opens the day and gathers the angels of both night and day.
rows.anchor: أن المراد نفسه صلاة الفجر وإنما أقسم بصلاة الفجر لأنها صلاة في مفتتح النهار وتجتمع لها ملائكة النهار وملائكة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn-prayer reading is supported by the statement that the dawn recitation is witnessed by angels of night and day.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view identifies a particular day's dawn; one proposal is the Day of Sacrifice, when pilgrimage rites distinctive to Abraham's religion and sacrifice occur.
rows.anchor: أنه فجر يوم النحر ، وذلك لأن أمر المناسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Sacrifice is explained by the worshipper's offering as a substitute for the self-sacrifice he cannot make.
rows.anchor: يأتي الإنسان فيه بالقربان كأن الحاج يريد أن يتقرب بذبح نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another particular-day view takes it as the dawn of Dhū al-Ḥijja, paired with the ten nights and marking the start of the month of the great rite.
rows.anchor: أراد فجر ذي الحجة لأنه قرن به قوله : { وليال عشر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view takes it as the dawn of Muḥarram, the first day of the year when recurring annual observances and lunar reckoning begin.
rows.anchor: المراد فجر المحرم ، أقسم به لأنه أول يوم من كل سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report calls Muḥarram the greatest month with God; al-Rāzī gives no chain or grading here.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر «أن أعظم الشهور عند الله المحرم »

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls Muḥarram the year's dawn, treating the whole month as a dawn.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه قال : فجر السنة هو المحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes al-fajr as the springs from which water gushes and which sustain living creatures.
rows.anchor: أنه عنى بالفجر العيون التي تنفجر منها المياه

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth explains jawb as cutting through something, like cutting an opening in a garment.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : الجواب قطعك الشيء كما يجاب الجيب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ adds the form yajib jayban and says that traversing a country is called jawb.
rows.anchor: وزاد الفراء يجيب جيبا ويقال :

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Thamūd cut through lands to make houses, pools, and whatever buildings they wanted.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كانوا يجوبون البلاد فيجعلون منها بيوتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī links this account of carving rock dwellings to the Qurʾānic statement that they carved houses from mountains.
rows.anchor: كما قال : { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says Thamūd were the first to quarry mountains, stone, and marble.
rows.anchor: قيل : أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same report says they built 1,700 cities, all of stone.
rows.anchor: وبنوا ألفا وسبعمائة مدينة كلها من الحجارة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil identifies the valley as Wādī al-Qurā.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : بوادي القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage connects to God's being in wait at the resurrection: people should strive for the afterlife, but this person cares only for worldly desires.
rows.anchor: قوله : { فأما الإنسان } متعلق بقوله : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person reads worldly comfort as God's honoring him and lack of comfort as God's humiliation of him.
rows.anchor: فإن وجد الراحة في الدنيا يقول : ربي أكرمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī compares this worldly outlook to people who know only the outward life of this world and neglect the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى في صفة الكفار : { يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also compares it to the person who worships God conditionally, content when blessed but turning away when tested.
rows.anchor: وقال : { ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First, worldly happiness is negligible beside afterlife happiness: worldly comfort ending in afterlife misery is no happiness, and worldly pain ending in salvation is no humiliation.
rows.anchor: أن سعادة الدنيا وشقاوتها في مقابلة ما في الآخرة من السعادة والشقاوة كالقطرة في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person therefore cannot decide that worldly ease proves final honor or that worldly suffering proves final disgrace.
rows.anchor: إذ المتنعم في الدنيا لا يجوز له أن يحكم على نفسه بالسعادة والكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second, worldly wealth and pain do not establish merit: God may expand for sinners or unbelievers by His will, for wise purposes, or as a means of entrapment, and may constrict the righteous for corresponding reasons.
rows.anchor: فإنه تعالى كثيرا ما يوسع على العصاة والكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither expansion nor constriction should be assumed to be recompense for what a person deserves.
rows.anchor: وقد يضيق على الصديقين لأضداد ما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third, those enjoying wealth must consider the final outcome; the poor must remember God's boundless gifts of bodily, intellectual, and religious well-being and protection from countless harms.
rows.anchor: والفقير والمحتاج لا ينبغي أن يغفل عما لله عليه من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poor person should not pronounce himself humiliated without qualification.
rows.anchor: فلا ينبغي أن يقضي على نفسه بالإهانة مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fourth, sensual habits and desires make attachment to worldly pleasures hard to break, while deprivation turns a person back to God and worship.
rows.anchor: أما إذا لم يحصل للإنسان شيء من هذه المحسوسات رجعت شاءت أم أبت إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finding the world may deprive one of closeness to God, while lacking it can be a means to the greatest happiness.
rows.anchor: فكان وجدان الدنيا سببا للحرمان من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fifth, lasting experience intensifies love, and stronger love makes separation more painful; abundant worldly enjoyment can therefore increase pain at death.
rows.anchor: أن كثرة الممارسة سبب لتأكد المحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conversely, less attachment may mean greater afterlife happiness, so possession is not necessarily happiness and deprivation is not necessarily misery.
rows.anchor: فإذن حصول لذات الدنيا سبب للألم الشديد بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These arguments presuppose belief in bodily or spiritual resurrection; someone denying every form of resurrection would otherwise have to equate possession with happiness and deprivation with misery.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الوجوه إنما تصح مع القول بإثبات البعث روحانيا كان أو جسمانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even one who denies resurrection cannot confidently judge by wealth alone, since great wealth may bring murder, robbery, and torment while deprivation may preserve safety.
rows.anchor: أنه ربما كان وجدان الدنيا الكثيرة سببا للقتل والنهب والوقوع في أنواع العذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One reported view says the human denotes two particular people: ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa and Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: فروي عن ابن عباس أنه عتبة بن ربيعة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the person as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : هو أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says the passage was revealed concerning Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other view takes 'the human' as anyone characterized by this description: an unbeliever who denies the Day of Recompense.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من كان موصوفا بهذا الوصف وهو الكافر الجاحد ليوم الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both expansion and restriction are tests: expansion tests gratitude or ingratitude, while restriction tests patience or despair.
rows.anchor: لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī compares these paired tests with the statement that God tests people with good and evil as a trial.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قوله تعالى : { ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible answer to the apparent rebuke is that 'No!' rejects only the claim that God humiliated the person in poverty.
rows.anchor: لأن كلمة الإنكار هي قوله : { كلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the rebuke covers both claims, one explanation is that the person assumes the wealth was deserved.
rows.anchor: سلمنا أن الإنكار عائد إليهما معا ولكن فيه وجوه ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that God's gifts of bodily health, reason, and religion preceded wealth; acknowledging blessing only upon gaining money shows boasting, not gratitude.
rows.anchor: أن نعم الله تعالى كانت حاصلة قبل وجدان المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Boasting of worldly gifts while ignoring afterlife blessings signals denial of resurrection, as in the owner of the garden who doubts the Hour.
rows.anchor: أن تصلفه بنعمة الدنيا وإعراضه عن ذكر نعمة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause uses fāʾ and the second wāw because mercy precedes anger and testing by blessings precedes testing by pain; the more frequent blessing is put first.
rows.anchor: لأن رحمة الله سابقة على غضبه وابتلاءه بالنعم سابق على ابتلائه بإنزال الآلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text says God honored the person but does not say He humiliated him: the first claim is true, while treating reduced provision as humiliation is false.
rows.anchor: لأنه في قوله : { أكرمن } صادق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting someone's provision means narrowing it to an amount sufficient for bare subsistence.
rows.anchor: ضيق عليه بأن جعله على مقدار البلغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read with a light or doubled dāl, both conveying that provision was tightened.
rows.anchor: وقرئ فقدر على التخفيف وبالتشديد أي قتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At pause, the final nūn of akramani and ahānani is unvocalized for readers who omit the yāʾ in connected speech and rely on its kasra.
rows.anchor: وأكرمن وأهانن بسكون النون في الوقف فيمن ترك الياء في الدرج مكتفيا منها بالكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage connects to God's being in wait at the resurrection: people should strive for the afterlife, but this person cares only for worldly desires.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other view takes 'the human' as anyone characterized by this description: an unbeliever who denies the Day of Recompense.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من كان موصوفا بهذا الوصف وهو الكافر الجاحد ليوم الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both expansion and restriction are tests: expansion tests gratitude or ingratitude, while restriction tests patience or despair.
rows.anchor: لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī compares these paired tests with the statement that God tests people with good and evil as a trial.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قوله تعالى : { ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible answer to the apparent rebuke is that 'No!' rejects only the claim that God humiliated the person in poverty.
rows.anchor: لأن كلمة الإنكار هي قوله : { كلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the rebuke covers both claims, one explanation is that the person assumes the wealth was deserved.
rows.anchor: سلمنا أن الإنكار عائد إليهما معا ولكن فيه وجوه ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that God's gifts of bodily health, reason, and religion preceded wealth; acknowledging blessing only upon gaining money shows boasting, not gratitude.
rows.anchor: أن نعم الله تعالى كانت حاصلة قبل وجدان المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Boasting of worldly gifts while ignoring afterlife blessings signals denial of resurrection, as in the owner of the garden who doubts the Hour.
rows.anchor: أن تصلفه بنعمة الدنيا وإعراضه عن ذكر نعمة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause uses fāʾ and the second wāw because mercy precedes anger and testing by blessings precedes testing by pain; the more frequent blessing is put first.
rows.anchor: لأن رحمة الله سابقة على غضبه وابتلاءه بالنعم سابق على ابتلائه بإنزال الآلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text says God honored the person but does not say He humiliated him: the first claim is true, while treating reduced provision as humiliation is false.
rows.anchor: لأنه في قوله : { أكرمن } صادق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting someone's provision means narrowing it to an amount sufficient for bare subsistence.
rows.anchor: ضيق عليه بأن جعله على مقدار البلغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read with a light or doubled dāl, both conveying that provision was tightened.
rows.anchor: وقرئ فقدر على التخفيف وبالتشديد أي قتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At pause, the final nūn of akramani and ahānani is unvocalized for readers who omit the yāʾ in connected speech and rely on its kasra.
rows.anchor: وأكرمن وأهانن بسكون النون في الوقف فيمن ترك الياء في الدرج مكتفيا منها بالكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the claim that worldly wealth proves honor or poverty proves contempt; God's allocation is not such a verdict.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما حكى عنهم تلك الشبهة قال : { كلا }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God does not test someone with riches because He honors him or with poverty because He despises him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المعنى لم ابتله بالغنى لكرامته علي

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: On the Sunni account presented here, allocation follows sheer decree, power, will, and judgment, which transcend causal explanations.
rows.anchor: بل ذلك إما على مذهب أهل السنة ، فمن محض القضاء

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: On the Muʿtazilite account, allocation follows hidden benefits that only God can know.
rows.anchor: وإما على مذهب المعتزلة فبسبب مصالح خفية لا يطلع عليها إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may expand an unbeliever's wealth without honoring him or restrict a believer without despising him.
rows.anchor: فقد يوسع على الكافر لا لكرامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people's conduct is worse than their mistaken claim: God gives them abundant wealth, yet they fail to honor the orphan.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قال : بل لهم فعل هو شر من هذا القول

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads this and the following verbs in the third person, matching al-insān as a collective, third-person expression.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو : { يكرمون } وما بعده بالياء المنقوطة من تحت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second-person reading is addressed by the Prophet to the people: 'Say this to them.'
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فالتقدير قل لهم يا محمد ذلك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil reports that Qudāma ibn Maẓʿūn was an orphan in the care of Umayya ibn Khalaf, who withheld his right.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : كان قدامة بن مظعون يتيما في حجر أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One form of failing to honor the orphan is neglecting kindness toward him, connected with the failure to urge feeding the poor.
rows.anchor: ترك بره ، وإليه الإشارة بقوله : { ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second form is withholding the orphan's inheritance and consuming his property, connected with devouring the estate.
rows.anchor: دفعه عن حقه الثابت له في الميراث وأكل ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third form is taking the orphan's money and joining it to one's own wealth.
rows.anchor: أي تأخذون أموال اليتامى وتضمونها إلى أموالكم
